artworks.title: American Green-Winged Teal
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paperr
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two American Green-winged Teals standing on rocks. The image features a male and a female teal, each showing distinct plumage patterns. The male has a red and green head, speckled grey and white breast and belly, and wings with shades of grey and dark green. The female has brown and tan feathering with subtle patterning. Both birds are standing on rocks with blades of grass emerging from the left. The painting is detailed and realistic, capturing the intricate feathers and features of the birds with precision.

artworks.title: Scaup Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two ducks. The duck on the left has dark blues, greens, and white colors, while the duck on the right is brown with lighter underbelly tones. Both ducks are surrounded by green, bending plant leaves.

artworks.title: Ruddy Plover
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two shorebirds foraging along a coastline. The image features two birds with light gray and white plumage, detailed feathers, and slender legs. They are depicted walking along what appears to be a sandy or rocky shore, surrounded by small shells and stones, with the ocean and two small islands visible in the background. The scene includes a clear blue sky.

artworks.title: Long-billed Curlew
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two long-billed curlews near a body of water with a distant cityscape in the background. The curlews are depicted standing together among tall grasses and rocks, with their elongated, curved bills prominently displayed. The background features a serene sky with light, wispy clouds and hints of color from a setting or rising sun. The scene is completed by a view of a city across the water, with buildings and spires adding to the horizon line. The artwork shows careful attention to the birds' plumage and the natural setting.

artworks.title: Hooded Merganser
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two hooded mergansers standing on a rocky outcrop by water. One is a male with a black and white crest, bold coloring, and intricate patterning, while the other is a smaller, subtler female with brown tones and a reddish crest. The birds are depicted on rocks with tufts of grass, next to blue water. The painting is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Sora or Rail
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows three birds in a natural setting with plants and grasses. The birds have brown, white, and black feathers with hints of blue and green, red eyes, and yellow bills. The scene features earthy tones and subtle blue hues. The birds are positioned from left to right - one walking with its head slightly downward, one stretching vertically with its beak open towards a blade of grass, and one pecking at the ground amidst vegetation.

artworks.title: Tufted Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two ducks, one brown and the other black and white, designed in an illustrative style. The color palette includes earthy browns, dark greens, creamy whites, and deep blacks. The brown duck is on the left, lying on the ground with its head slightly up. The black and white duck is on the right, standing with its head turned upwards. They are on a patch of ground with sparse grass and rocks.

artworks.title: Sooty Tern
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Sooty Tern in flight. The bird has its wings spread wide, soaring through the sky. The plumage is primarily a dark shade contrasting with the lighter sky and clouds in the background. The feathers are detailed, capturing their texture and natural patterning. The bird's open beak reveals a hint of pink inside. The style is similar to John James Audubon, known for detailed bird illustrations. The overall effect is of grace and freedom, capturing the essence of this seabird in motion.

artworks.title: Night Heron or Qua bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two herons in a natural setting. The black-crowned night heron and its juvenile are surrounded by tall grass, flowers, and a water source. The adult heron is shown with its head lowered, near a small frog. The juvenile heron, with streaked brown plumage, stands among greenery and white flowers. The painting is in the style of John James Audubon, showcasing avian anatomy and habitat.

artworks.title: Great Esquimaux Curlew
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a brown bird with a long, slightly curved beak, standing on a rocky surface with grass in the background. The bird is depicted in profile, displaying its detailed plumage pattern, a light underbelly, and striped tail feathers. The grass behind it is lush, painted in various shades of green.

artworks.title: Great Marbled Godwit
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds standing among tall grasses. The artwork features two birds with long beaks, standing on the ground. Their plumage includes muted browns, creams, and subtle reds with detailed feather textures. The bird in the foreground has its beak slightly forward, while the one behind has its wings raised. The background shows lush greenery, including grass and leafy plants. The style resembles that of John James Audubon, known for attention to naturalistic detail and vibrancy in avian subjects.

artworks.title: American Coot
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of an American Coot by the water's edge, surrounded by tall grasses. The bird's black plumage contrasts sharply with its pale green legs and striking red eyes, as it stands on a muddy bank next to the clear blue water. Tall, lush green grasses form the backdrop. The detailing in the bird's feathers and feet, as well as in the delicate strands of grass, showcases a careful observation of nature. This is in style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Roseate Tern
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a roseate tern in flight. The bird is depicted with its wings spread wide as it swoops downward, its detailed feathers rendered in shades of gray and white with hints of pink near the throat. The beak is red and the eyes are intense. The background is a smooth, solid blue.

artworks.title: Black-Backed Gull
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Black-Backed Gull depicted in great detail. The bird is shown in a dynamic pose with its wings extended upward, displaying its dark upper feathers. Its head is turned back with its mouth open. Below the bird, hints of a rocky ground surface can be seen, adding texture to the image. A single gull's foot is illustrated separately in the upper right corner. The attention to detail in the bird's plumage and the naturalistic setting reflect an emphasis on ornithological precision. This painting is done in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Snowy Heron, or White Egret
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: A white bird with long legs, a long neck, and a narrow, pointed beak stands facing our right in profile against a deep landscape in this vertical, colored engraving. Feathers lying close to the neck and body resemble long, soft hair cascading down and off the back of the head, off the bottom of the neck where it meets the body, and around the tail. The bird’s beak and legs are black, and the eye we see and its feet are pale yellow. It stands on a dirt-packed riverbank in front of tall grasses. Grassy fields lead into the deep distance to the right, where a house and outbuildings sit on the horizon about a third of the way up the composition. A person carrying a rifle approaches the riverbank from the far side of a hill near the lower right corner of the print. Thin gray clouds skirt across a mostly blue sky above. Text is printed beneath the image: “Drawn from Nature, by J.J. Audubon. F.R.S. F.L.S.” to the left; “Snowy Heron, or White Egret, Ardea Candidissima, Gm. Male adult spring plumage River Plantation, South Carolina” in the center; and “Engraved, Printed, & Coloured by R. Havell, London. 1835.” to the right.

artworks.title: American Snipe
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image depicts three snipe birds in a natural setting. The birds are shown in detail interacting with each other. One bird is slightly larger than the others and is standing among reeds. The background shows a calm body of water reflecting the sky, with trees and a house in the distance. The color palette is Earthy with browns and greens for the birds and vegetation, while the water and sky are in muted blues and grays.

artworks.title: Common Gallinule
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird standing near a body of water. The image portrays a bird with a dark body and distinctive bright red beak and frontal shield, walking on long greenish legs with large feet. It is depicted with one foot forward, positioned on a grassy patch near some water. The background shows a body of water with some rocks and reeds along the shoreline. The detail and style suggest a focus on ornithological accuracy. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Uria Brunnichii
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is an image of a bird in flight over water. The bird has dark feathers on its back and wings, and white feathers underneath. It has a black beak, red eyes, and webbed feet. The background shows a gradient from light to dark, resembling a sky, with waves in the water below. The painting is detailed, focusing on the bird's feathers. It is reminiscent of the style of John James Audubon, known for detailed bird illustrations.

artworks.title: Eider Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of eider ducks in a natural setting. The image features three ducks amid lush grasses. The ducks’ feathers are rendered in detailed, natural colors, with notable variations in pattern across the different birds. The background is a mix of sky and dense foliage.

artworks.title: Velvet Duck
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting features two ducks on a rocky shore. One duck is resting and the other is standing. The duck on the left has brown feathers with white patches on its face and sides, pink legs, and webbed feet. The duck on the right has a dark body, a white patch near its wings, and an orange bill. Both ducks are on rocks with a hint of water in the background. The painting showcases detailed textures and precision in the ducks' anatomy, following the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Razor Bill
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting featuring two razorbill birds floating on the water near a rocky coastline. The painting depicts two birds with black feathers on their heads, backs, and tails, and white underbellies. One bird has its beak open, displaying its bright yellow interior, while the other bird appears calm. The setting includes a body of teal water with gentle waves, and in the background, there is a jagged rocky landscape under a pale sky. The text at the bottom of the painting indicates the artist's name, as well as the bird species' name. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Puffin
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two puffins in a coastal setting. The scene features one puffin standing on a rocky outcrop while another peeks out from a burrow nestled in grassy terrain. The puffin standing outside showcases its colorful beak and red feet, along with its black and white plumage. The background includes a body of water leading to distant landforms under a pale sky. This illustration is detailed and scientific.

artworks.title: Common Gull
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two gulls, one with lighter plumage and the other with a mottled brown and white pattern. The color palette includes grays, browns, and white, with hints of yellow and pink. The light-colored gull is on the left, facing upward and slightly to the right, while the brown gull is on the right, facing the viewer. In the foreground, there are multicolored shells on the ground.

artworks.title: American Pied-Bill Dobchick
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two American Pied-bill Dobchicks swimming in a body of water surrounded by lush greenery. The painting depicts two birds swimming closely together, their sleek brown and white bodies partially submerged in the water. They have sharp beaks and are positioned in a dynamic diagonal that guides the viewer's eye from the foreground to the background, through a lush array of green, leaf-filled plants. The background is rich with dense vegetation, featuring long, elegant reeds and a small branch with a slightly twisted form adding variety to the scene.
